summary: The service started this run, not an instruction: the width-200 nudge loop at f* 0.38 (job 164681, E0075) had ended. There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered, and no time went to unasked work. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claims or blockers are open on this line. My one point from the last review was answered: the sentence 'width 200 never reached further' is narrowed in evidence/E0076-results.json, the line state, PROGRAM.md and progress.md, and the new wording is right. The collected numbers reproduce exactly. All fifty-two per-step entries for this loop in evidence/E0076-interim.json match the mirrored summary.json files: SHA-256, Gamma, outcome, cycles, CPU-hours, energy gains, audit failures and slow stretches, with zero mismatches. There are fifty completed steps. The steps sum to 74.68 CPU-hours, against 75.1 in the job record. The floor stop is a two CPU-hour cap at Gamma 2.4 after twenty-four cycles. At 4.4 time froze in the twenty-fifth cycle, at 6.51 CPU-hours, under the eight-hour cap. No step slowed, gained energy or failed the audit, so the referee check on slow stretches is clean: the loop never slowed before its stall. The width-100 comparison (E0065, f* 0.38) reproduces: floor 2.25 with a cap stop at 2.2 after seventeen cycles, top 4.35 with a cap stop at 4.4 after nineteen. The cost per cycle at 4.4 against 4.35 is 2.5 times at width 200 and 1.86 times at width 100. I recomputed the matched-step cost ratios from E0065 and the mirror and got the same medians: 7.6 going down (eleven pairs) and 10.26 going up (thirty-eight pairs). Three sentences are wrong. (1) The summary's takeaway says both boxes stopped at 4.4, 'the same step where every nudge loop in the paper's box stopped on Nov 18'. That is false. In evidence/E0065-results.json, five of the eight width-100 nudge loops that started stopped at 4.45 (f* 0.84 to 0.50), two at 4.4 (0.44 and 0.38) and one at 4.5 (0.33), all on their CPU caps. The Nov 18 finding in PROGRAM.md itself says 'a wall going up at Gamma 4.35 to 4.45'. The sentence is not in the line state, which only compares f* 0.38, so the dashboard is not affected. (2) The summary says 'The caps were scaled only four times.' That holds for the down leg (2.0 against 0.5 CPU-hours). It is wrong for the up leg: the width-200 up cap was 8.0 CPU-hours against width 100's 0.5, so it was scaled sixteen times, more than the measured cost ratio of about ten. (3) Because of (2), proposed direction two ('scale the width-200 step caps by the measured cost ratio, about seven and a half going down, ten going up') is half wrong. The up cap already exceeds ten times, so only the down caps were too small. Scaling the up caps to ten times would lower them. An up-cap proposal was also withdrawn in an earlier run. One consequence for the reading of the top: width 200 got a relatively larger budget at 4.4 than width 100 (sixteen times the cap for about ten to twenty-six times the cost per cycle, 977 against 94.9 CPU-seconds), so 'one-sided' is the right word and the run uses it. The line state's 'the wall at Gamma 4.4 is there in the wider box too' rests on a stall at width 200 and a cap stop at width 100. Read with E0085, which found the width-100 wall at 4.4 at f* 0.44, it is fair for this f*, but only for this f*. The run ended at 09:37:37Z and was committed at 09:38:05Z, and when I checked at 09:40:53Z that time was still in the future. The timestamps are wrong and should be corrected to the real time. program check passes. The latest approval is still approved/20261124T031934297997Z (Nov 24 03:19), so none were made in the last day. It counts 561.4 of 10000 weekly CPU-hours. My last count of 801.5 for ended jobs plus this job's 75.1 gives about 877, so the run's 'about 875' is right, and program check still undercounts. sequel-data is 683 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 91 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. active.jsonl is empty. sequel-data/tmp/ is not empty: it holds dbg.py, frozen.log, layer.py and one.py. These were written between 09:39:40 and 09:40:43Z, after this run ended, and they are two-dimensional held-contact tests. They belong to another line's session, not to this run. Outside the two allowed folders, the only writes in the window are the harness's own folders and ~/.tmp (TMPDIR). As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a three-and-a-half-minute service run, from 09:34:04 to 09:37:37 by its own record, committed at 09:38:05. It started about two minutes after the service recorded the ended job at 09:31:51. It collected the one ended loop, compared it with the width-100 nudge loop and answered my one point. It started nothing, cancelled nothing and left no local jobs. Eighteen width-200 loops are still on Hatteras: ten without friction (E0074) and eight with the nudge (E0075). The host is a Linux container, so pmset and uptime are unavailable and sleep could not be measured, as the summary says. Local CPU of 0.01 hours fits a run of reading and writing. Free disk of 91 gigabytes at both ends matches what I see. The machine did not limit the science. The loop's own step caps set both floors, and the summary says this is a limit of the design. The job's 75.1 CPU-hours are under the 100 CPU-hour per-run limit.
